title: Canadian Poplar: Old Poplars You Can Visit
meta_description: A hybrid bred for timber and never meant to last. The Netherlands' oldest poplar has stood behind an Arnhem concert hall since the 1700s.
intro: Canadian poplar is a hybrid of Europe's black poplar and an American cottonwood, bred for timber and shelter belts: fast, soft, and usually felled within decades rather than left for centuries. The old ones are the trees somebody forgot to take out. The oldest poplar in the Netherlands grows behind a concert hall in Arnhem, on the last stretch of moat the city never filled in, and has stood since somewhere between 1750 and 1800. Amsterdam's in the Vondelpark has reached about 38 metres on the edge of a bicycle path. Leeuwarden's Marilandica, a named clone, has a trunk so covered in burrs that it reads closer to rock than bark. Warsaw's was already mature when the ground it stands on became a transit camp in 1944, and Antwerp's runs six metres of clear trunk before the crown starts.
